title: 🔧 Databricks' Agent Fixes Broken Data Pipelines on Its Own — and Turns the Diagnosis into a Pull Request!
body: 🔧 Databricks' Agent Fixes Broken Data Pipelines on Its Own — and Turns the Diagnosis into a Pull Request!

Databricks opened the public beta of its Genie Zero Ops agent — an AI agent that monitors data pipelines in the background, detects failures and quality problems, diagnoses their cause, and then proposes a ready fix. The company said the agent was designed and trained on lessons drawn from more than 80,000 real problems its customers faced in their data pipelines.

The agent works in five consecutive steps without anyone writing a single command: it detects a failure or a silent problem, such as a table that was not updated or a load missing rows; then gathers context from logs, code, metadata, and lineage tracking; then tests the proposed fix in an isolated environment; then sends a brief alert to the team; and finally turns the diagnosis into a pull request ready for review. A workspace administrator can enable the feature from the previews page, and the new version includes a shared team inbox and custom instructions for the agent.

Most importantly, the agent never changes any code or data on its own; every fix remains a proposal on a new branch until a human approves it. The company first introduced the idea in June, then tested it with hundreds of companies in a private preview, before opening it to all customers now.

Simply put: imagine a vigilant maintenance technician who never sleeps, watching the data pipes — and when he finds a leak, he pinpoints its location, prepares the spare part, and leaves it for you to approve; that is what the new agent does, without touching anything before your permission.
Would you be comfortable with an AI agent monitoring your company's data and proposing fixes, or do you prefer maintenance to stay fully human?
